title: A p-independent family extends to a p-basis
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of fields of characteristic $p$. Let $K^p=\{b^p:b\in K\}$ and let $kK^p$ be the subfield of $K$ generated by $k$ and $K^p$. For a family $(z_l)_{l\in\Lambda}$ of elements of $K$ and $E=(e_l)_{l\in\Lambda}$ a family of integers with $0\le e_l<p$ for all $l$ and $e_l=0$ for all but finitely many $l$, write $z^E=\prod_{l\in\Lambda}z_l^{e_l}$. Let $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of elements of $K$ which is $p$-independent over $k$: the monomials $x^E$ (as a family indexed by $E$) are linearly independent over $kK^p$. Then there are a set $J$ and a family $(y_j)_{j\in J}$ of elements of $K$ such that the combined family $(z_l)_{l\in I\sqcup J}$, with $z_i=x_i$ for $i\in I$ and $z_j=y_j$ for $j\in J$, is a $p$-basis of $K$ over $k$: the monomials $z^E$ form a basis of the $kK^p$-vector space $K$.

proof.text: Independence of the monomial family makes x injective: compare the exponent functions single i 1 and single j 1, which are bounded because p>1. Reindex exponent functions along I equivalent to range x using Finsupp.equivCongrLeft. This preserves products and yields independence of the image subset.

proof.text: If a is outside the monomial span, the insertion theorem makes insert a T independent. Maximality puts a in T. But the exponent function single a 1 is bounded, so a itself is in the monomial range and therefore in its span, a contradiction. Thus the monomial span is top.

proof.text: Take J={a in T : a not in range x} and y the inclusion. The combined map I disjoint union J to T is injective by injectivity of x and disjointness of the images, and surjective by splitting membership in range x. Construct its equivalence with Equiv.ofBijective. Reindex bounded exponent functions by Finsupp.equivCongrLeft and transport the basis built by Module.Basis.mk from independence and spanning. Finsupp.prod_equivMapDomain proves the requested evaluation formula.
